Official v1.5.0 `f9a26365` after-run assertions now pass selected runtime paths at `e716c0b6025819c5d5b19c5dff8f46e2ab18e2b8` and live in `durable/harness_after_run_main_test.go`.

The two fixtures previously held here were re-run against the current package with the continuation prototype excluded only in the compiler input, and passed unchanged, so they are promoted: `harness_after_run_orphan_test.go` is now `durable/harness_after_run_orphan_main_test.go` (source 785), and `harness_after_run_selection_test.go` is now `durable/harness_after_run_selection_main_test.go` (source 882 and 903). Assertions were not weakened; the `WaitForIdle` cancellation witness in the orphan fixture records that public idle settlement stays unsettled while the missing-definition child is blocked. Five functions, `-count=1`: five passes, zero failures/skips, 0.510s. The pinned source case that gives a run without a recorded first entry its answer as first (source 957) cannot be ported: it mutates the live run document inside a hook, and native public `Tx` exposes only `CreateTask`, so no document-write path exists without expanding the public API. No runtime change was made for it. The typed hook replaces the declaration-only adapter, which was removed. [Runtime assertions and remaining source work](../../../../docs/upstream-v1.5.0/after-run.md) retain scope and native adapters; the [historical baseline](../../../../docs/upstream-v1.5.0/after-run-baseline.md) keeps its original failures/recipe at5a08638 and all29 source declarations. Full after-run/body parity is unverified.

The remaining fixture here is `harness_after_run_history_test.go` (source 694), a known-failing oracle run through the project overlay with the protected prototype replaced only in the compiler input: `go test -overlay <run>/overlay.json ./durable -run '^TestMainAfterRunHookHistoryKeepsRunStartHiddenByMidRunCompaction' -count=1 -timeout=90s` in `$PROJECT_TMP_ROOT/runs/after-run-oracle/20261103/`. It fails on the first assertion — the `afterRun` hook is never invoked for a run whose answer follows a model tool round, so the history checks are not reached. The failure is not a selection artifact: it reproduces with the extension selected explicitly on the agent, and with no gate and no compaction, so the tool-round continuation itself skips the hook. The pinned contract (pinned generation.ts864 `answer()` evaluates `asksAfterRun` before the answer commit) requires the hook to run there; native `handoffToolGeneration` carries no afterRun state into the successor checkpoint, and the post-tool answer commit does not evaluate the hook selection. Root cause is narrowed but not fully pinned. The source's ordered kind sequence needs `api.entries(minEntryId..maxEntryId)`; the native `HookAPI` exposes no range scan, so that assertion is not ported, and no API expansion was made.

Future known-failing fixtures belong here only with an explicit project-owned execution recipe, prototype exclusion, retained complete assertions and a concise baseline receipt. Never use a default skip or relaxed expected count to hide a failure.
